article.name: Hatchdoor
article.summary: Hatchdoor is a self-hosted Markdown vault server with browser and MCP interfaces. Markdown files are canonical and a disposable SQLite cache supports browsing, links, metadata, keyword search, and semantic search. The review describes inspected source mechanisms; no runtime quality or benchmark result was measured.

who_what.text: The official repository presents Hatchdoor as a self-hosted Markdown/Obsidian-vault server with browser and MCP interfaces. The README describes it as a private single-trusted-user deployment rather than a multi-user collaboration service.
The official repository page identifies BatterWorks/Hatchdoor and default branch main; the official commits/main API identifies the reviewed full head.

architecture.text: The runtime combines HTTP, MCP, and browser surfaces over shared Vault read and mutation cores. A Vault registry identifies each Markdown source folder and its optional Git configuration; the source tree is authoritative and the shared SQLite cache is disposable.

A published Vault snapshot holds note structure, links, tags, metadata, and searchable chunks. Snapshot freshness, participation, and vector searchability are modeled independently; structural browsing can be available before embeddings are ready.
The shared search implementation exposes keyword and semantic modes. Search results retain Vault and note identity, path, heading, content, score, layer, links, and metadata.

behavior.text: The mutation core resolves a single Vault, checks lifecycle and write capability, serializes mutations with that Vault's lock, builds an index for path/layer validation, and executes filesystem work off the async runtime. The exported APIs cover note creation, append/edit/update/frontmatter/section changes, move/rename, archive, deletion, tags, and attachments.

Writes carry an expected content hash to refuse stale edits. Atomic compare-and-swap is available where the filesystem supports it; otherwise the documented code path uses a weaker check-then-rename flow that may race an outside editor. An intent log supports recovery after interrupted multi-file writes.

Delete moves a note and its folder assets into .hatchdoor-trash, which indexing excludes; archive moves the note under a configured prefix. These moves do not establish physical or remote-copy erasure.
Read APIs include exact note reads, outlines/sections, browse views, and search. Keyword and semantic search are selected as separate modes, and search bounds candidate ranking and results per note.
VaultScope accepts one canonical Vault ID or all. The read projection excludes nonparticipating Vault snapshots and search carries selected Vault IDs into its cache queries; writes target one Vault.

metrics.evidence: Keyword/semantic search and exact reads are present in source; answer correctness and abstention were not evaluated.
Hash-checked updates and fresh/stale snapshot state exist; correction accuracy and stale-answer rate were not measured.
Delete moves notes into excluded trash; no post-delete retrieval, remote-copy, or Git-history probe was run.
Vault-qualified scopes and cache filters are implemented; no isolation workload was run, and the documented shared-user model is not per-user authorization.
The system exposes note paths, links, metadata, and optional Git origin labels; answer evidence support was not adjudicated.
Search bounds and index progress exist, but no latency or end-to-end freshness timing was collected.
Compact result shapes and local embedding options are documented; no token/cost workload was run.
SQLite is a rebuildable read model over Markdown; no size or rebuild-cost comparison was made.

limits.text: The README documents a single trusted-user deployment: whoever can reach the instance can access its served Vaults. One shared MCP bearer token and caller-supplied client names do not establish individual identity or per-Vault authorization.
Delete moves content into trash and optional Git history/remotes may retain other copies. The reviewed sources and this inspection do not establish secure erasure across backups or remotes.

This bounded review inspected the README, module map, shared mutation/read cores, scoped search, snapshot storage, Git origin messages and security policy. It did not inspect every adapter, helper, cache migration or model path. No runtime, tests, benchmarks, or isolation probes were run.

benchmark.note: No Hatchdoor runtime, tests, or benchmark workload was run; no metric is claimed.
